note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Reconciling debate theories motivates selective leader-centric LASE and its theoretical/empirical support

nodes.name: Corrective regime theory
nodes.description: Hu et al. (2025) show that when at least one agent produces a correct seed, debate acts as Bayesian posterior updating that amplifies correctness and can outperform majority vote.

nodes.name: Neutral regime theory
nodes.description: Choi et al. (2025) show that under symmetric information flow, Dirichlet belief updates form a martingale with zero expected improvement, so majority voting can dominate.

nodes.name: Debate is regime-dependent
nodes.description: The two theories are compatible: debate is corrective when asymmetric signals such as a correct seed exist and neutral when agents are symmetric with unconstrained information flow, so the question is when and how to invoke debate.

nodes.name: Uniform debate wastes compute
nodes.description: Existing frameworks apply debate uniformly across instances, conflating corrective and neutral regimes and incurring computational overhead where expected contribution is minimal.

nodes.name: Leader-supporter structure breaks symmetry
nodes.description: LASE uses a designated leader that synthesizes auxiliary critiques from supporters through a directed 1:1 star topology, forcing the system into the corrective regime with positive expected drift.

nodes.name: Uncertainty gating
nodes.description: LASE invokes interaction only when the leader's initial response is uncertain (U=1), judged from min logprob and max entropy signals, stopping early when U=0.

nodes.name: Calibration of uncertainty proxies
nodes.description: On MATH-500 (2,000 samples), accuracy is 85.5% for high-confidence generations (min logprob at least 0.99) versus 50.9% below 0.50, and falls to 30.4% when entropy exceeds 1.0.

nodes.name: Selective debate improves expected accuracy
nodes.description: Under the seed-conditional assumptions, LASE accuracy is at least leader-only accuracy plus P(U=1)*rho*delta (Theorem 3.7).

nodes.name: LASE costs less than static debate
nodes.description: LASE expected cost equals leader cost plus P(U=1) times one peer interaction, which is strictly below static debate cost whenever P(U=1)<1.

nodes.name: Star topology scales better
nodes.description: A leader-centric 1:1 scheme grows as O(T) cross-agent context inclusions versus Theta(T n^2) for all-to-all debate, an Omega(n^2) reduction.

nodes.name: LASE Pareto-dominates static debate
nodes.description: LASE strictly improves expected cost over static debate while keeping positive expected accuracy gain over leader-only inference (Corollary 3.9).

nodes.name: Accuracy gains over MV and MAD
nodes.description: On Gemini-2.0-Flash and GPT-4.1-mini, LASE outperforms majority voting and multi-agent debate, e.g. 65.2% on GPQA-Diamond versus MV 62.7% and MAD 62.1%, and 87.2% on MATH-500.

nodes.name: Over 10x token reduction
nodes.description: LASE cuts average token usage by over 10x versus MAD, e.g. 0.4k versus 5.6k on GSM-Symbolic (14x) and 1.1k versus MAD 11.8k and MV 5.2k on MATH-500.

nodes.name: Orthogonal to majority voting
nodes.description: Running LASE five times in parallel with majority voting adds +0.8% over single-path LASE, uses tokens comparable to MV with N=7, and significantly outperforms MV.

isolated_nodes.name: Permutation invariance
isolated_nodes.description: Randomly permuting agent order yields 86.9% (std 0.31) versus 87.2% main result on MATH-500, with stable ~1.1k tokens, so LASE is effectively permutation invariant.

isolated_nodes.name: Evaluation setup
isolated_nodes.description: Evaluation uses six benchmarks (MATH-500, MATH-lv5 N=1,324, GSM-Symbolic N=500, MMLU-Pro N=504, GPQA-Diamond N=198, TruthfulQA-MC N=817) against Single Agent, MV (N=7) and MAD (N=3, 2 rounds) baselines.

structural_reasoning: Theory reconciliation -> design of selective leader-centric debate -> theoretical guarantees and empirical validation. Robustness and setup isolated.
